artists.biography:
Crowded House are a pop rock band formed in Melbourne, Australia in 1985 by lead-vocalist and primary songwriter, New Zealand-born Neil Finn. Other members have included his brother Tim Finn, Australians Paul Hester, Nick Seymour and Peter Jones and Americans Mark Hart and Matt Sherrod.
Crowded House has won several national and international awards. In Australia, the group has won eleven ARIA Awards from 26 nominations, including the inaugural Best New Talent award in 1987. The majority of their ARIAs were awarded for their first two albums, Crowded House and Temple of Low Men. They won eight APRA Awards from eleven nominations and were nominated for The New Zealand Silver Scroll for "Don't Stop Now" in 2007.
"Don't Dream It's Over" was named the seventh best Australian song of all time in 2001.

perplexity.description:
The album Crowded House by the band Crowded House was originally released in June 1986 under Capitol Records. It is a pop album characterized by melodic songwriting and a blend of rock and pop sensibilities, featuring Neil Finn's distinctive vocals and thoughtful lyrics. The sound combines catchy hooks with introspective themes, establishing the band's signature style that balances accessibility with emotional depth.

As the band's debut album, Crowded House marked a significant entry in their discography, introducing them to international audiences. It includes notable singles such as "Don't Dream It's Over" and "Something So Strong," which contributed to the album's commercial success. The album peaked at number 2 on the Australian charts and achieved platinum certification in the United States, reflecting both critical acclaim and strong sales. This release laid the foundation for Crowded House's enduring reputation in the pop and rock music scenes.
